- When sentiment is consistently negative (≥15 days), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 7–14 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak for 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 45.00), model overreacts; adjust downward by 1–3% per day until trend stabilizes.  
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive (e.g., 1.00 after -1.00), model delays correction; add 1–2 days lag in downward adjustment.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the window; apply 1–3% downward bias for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend (e.g., 3 consecutive days <40.00), model fails to recognize it; apply 2–5% downward bias for next 5–10 days.
